revisions.reason: Review 20261118 NFS3 host-step lifetime: the existing parallel main/sibling Worker rendezvous owns one ThreadManager activity token from immediately before its try through its finally. The liveness closure checks this running host and pause/stop/frozen state. The token does not survive settlement, rejection or backend replacement and does not invoke guest exports, callbacks, polling, wake, focus or clocks. Actual native separate-UI/Device2 normal-Worker pressure control keeps native UI samples fresh while the main Worker synchronously waits on the real render Worker; callback admission and broader ownership remain pending. Run 20261118-nfs3-reviewed-frame-native-scene-latency.

revisions.reason: Review 20261118 explicit Worker host-step lifetime: retain the existing normal free-run dispatch and satisfied-wait paths while their exact backend owns a live awaited host rendezvous, even when its main native slice exceeds the 250ms no-new-step cutoff. The token captures backend identity and the host liveness predicate; stopped, stopping, replaced, paused and completed owners cannot inherit activity. Finally release is identity checked and idempotent; nested acquisition refuses. Outside a token the existing stale-step cutoff remains unchanged. No clock timestamp renewal, guest export, callback target, context restoration, timer, forced message probe, input, render or native scene freshness change. Focused scheduler/lifetime negatives and actual native old/new software-Device2 pressure controls are retained in run 20261118-nfs3-reviewed-frame-native-scene-latency. General callback ownership remains pending.
